chunks: And from him, from Safwan and Ibn Abi Umayr, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Pray them [the two dawn prayers] after the dawn rises.' There is no contradiction between these hadiths and what we presented before them, because the option and the command to pray after the dawn and with the dawn in these reports is directed only to one who did not manage to include them in the night prayer. And in none of them is it stated that it is not permissible before the dawn; rather, in many of them it is stated that he prays before and after and with [it]. It is also possible that what is meant by 'with the dawn' and 'after the dawn' is the first dawn, which rises upward, without it being meant the second dawn which spreads across the sky of heaven, which reveals what we mentioned. What was narrated is:

key_terms.صَلِّهِمَا: Pray them (referring to the two dawn prayers)

ai.seo_question: When is the best time to pray the two Fajr prayers according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi resolves the apparent discrepancy in narrations by distinguishing between the general permissibility of praying the two Fajr prayers before dawn and the specific recommendation for those who missed them during the night to perform them after the first dawn (al-fajr al-awwal). This interpretation aligns with the Shia understanding of flexibility in supererogatory timings, ensuring that the command to pray 'with' or 'after' dawn is seen as a directive for catch-up rather than a strict prohibition against earlier performance.
